evals.name: file-a-breakdown-ticket-completely
evals.prompt:
Working against the repo at /home/user/harness-ref (real repo; do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there) — read its harness.yaml to see which tracker backend is configured and where.

A proposal was accepted and broke down into three pieces. The second one is: "the push guard accepts a clean two-parent merge over a certified ancestor". It cannot start until the first piece (the gate record moves to a git ref) is done. It's ordinary priority.

Write me the exact sequence of operations to file this ticket, for this repo's configured backend. Don't run anything — write the sequence, with the actual commands. Save it as filing.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating tracker judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The sequence sets exactly one assurance label on the ticket
The sequence places the ticket in Todo as an explicit step, not as a side effect of creating it
The sequence sets the blocked-by relationship in the tracker's own field, not in the ticket's prose
The sequence sets the priority field
The final step verifies the result by re-reading the ticket rather than by trusting the exit status of the write
The commands are correct for the backend this repo's harness.yaml actually declares
The ticket body is passed as a file rather than interpolated into the shell command

evals.name: hold-a-ticket
evals.prompt:
Unattended run against /home/user/harness-ref (real repo; do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). I picked up a ticket and can't finish it: it needs a credential I don't have — the board token isn't in the environment.

What do I do to the ticket so the loop doesn't pick it up again, and so the operator sees why? Give me the exact operations for this repo's backend. Save it as hold.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating tracker judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The answer applies all three parts of a hold: a comment, a label, and assignment to a human
It picks the correct one of the two hold labels for a missing credential and says why that one
It states that assignment is the part the loop's skip actually reads
It verifies the hold by re-reading the ticket
It does not invent a third hold label or a new state
It says the credential comes from the environment and is never written into the ticket or a comment

evals.name: append-to-the-improvement-ledger
evals.prompt:
A review on /home/user/harness-ref (real repo; do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there) turned up a non-blocking improvement that's too large to do in the branch: the tracker transport guidance prescribes commands that don't work when the host blocks GraphQL.

Where does this go, and how? Give me the operations. Save it as ledger.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating tracker judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The improvement is appended to an improvement ledger rather than filed as a ticket
The ledger is found by its label rather than by a hard-coded issue number
The answer says to create the ledger, with that label, if the search finds none
The answer says that exactly one open ledger per repo is expected and that finding two is reported rather than resolved by picking one
It states that the improvement also appears as one line in the review's own report
It distinguishes this from filing a bug, and states the test that separates the two — whether the tree contradicts its own contract today
